title: Organ Systems Working Together
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Organ Systems Working Together Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: The digestive, respiratory and circulatory systems work together to supply cells with nutrients and oxygen and remove wastes; keeping these systems healthy. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 1: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Life Science): the respiratory system, the circulatory system, gas exchange, the digestive system and digestion and enzymes. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The heart pumps blood; the lungs exchange gases.
key_sub: Food is digested and absorbed in the small intestine.
body_html:
How to think about it

The heart pumps blood through arteries (away from the heart), capillaries and veins (back to the heart). Blood carries oxygen, food and wastes. In the lungs, oxygen diffuses from the alveoli into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.

Digestion breaks food down: the mouth (teeth and saliva), osophagus, stomach (acid and enzymes), small intestine (digestion and absorption through villi) and large intestine (water is absorbed). Enzymes speed up digestion.

Example

Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?

A for away

Answer: arteries

Example

Where are most nutrients absorbed?

A long tube with villi

Answer: the small intestine

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the lungs pump blood.
  • Thinking food is absorbed in the stomach.
  • Thinking veins carry only oxygen-poor blood (the pulmonary vein does not).

faq.q: Why does your breathing get faster when you exercise?
faq.a: Your muscles need more oxygen and produce more carbon dioxide.

faq.q: Why do the alveoli have thin walls?
faq.a: So that gases can diffuse across them quickly.

items.q: Which gas do we breathe out more of than we breathe in?
items.e: Cells make carbon dioxide as waste.

items.q: What does an asthma inhaler do?
c: It opens up the airways so air can flow more easily.
items.e: Medical technology helps people breathe.

items.q: When you breathe out, what happens to the ribcage?
items.e: Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostals contract, ribs up and out, volume up, pressure down, air rushes in.

items.q: Where does air come from just before it reaches the trachea (windpipe)?
items.e: Nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.

items.q: What path does air take into the lungs?

items.e: Air travels down the windpipe.

items.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?

items.e: Exercise increases heart rate.

items.q: What is the main job of the mouth?

It absorbs water and mineral salts from undigested food.
Teeth break food into small pieces and saliva starts to digest starch.
It completes digestion and absorbs digested food into the blood.
items.e: The mouth: Teeth break food into small pieces and saliva starts to digest starch.
